ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Attack, CardRarity.Common, TargetType.AnyEnemy)` (TwinStrike.cs:18-21) == cost 1 / ATTACK / COMMON / ANY_ENEMY.

CanonicalTags.rationale: `new HashSet<CardTag> { CardTag.Strike }` (TwinStrike.cs:14) == the tag set that card/perfected_strike counts.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new DamageVar(5m, ValueProp.Move)` (TwinStrike.cs:16) == `_damage = 5`; the hit count of 2 is a literal `WithHitCount(2)` (26) and the sim stores it as `_hits = 2` so `base_hits` reports it.

OnPlay.rationale: `DamageCmd.Attack(5).WithHitCount(2).FromCard(this).Targeting(cardPlay.Target)` (TwinStrike.cs:26-29) == the sim's two-iteration loop of `DamageCmd.deal`. The per-hit `if target.is_gone or ctx.player.is_dead: break` is the correct analogue of AttackCommand's own breaks (AttackCommand.cs:540-550) -- it skips further HITS rather than a separate effect, so it carries no CanReceivePowers finding.

OnUpgrade.rationale: `DynamicVars.Damage.UpgradeValueBy(2m)` (TwinStrike.cs:34) == `self._damage += 2` (5 -> 7 PER HIT, so 14 total -- the per-hit reading is what the source says and the sim matches).
